execute_phase.stderr_excerpt: Some tensors share memory, this will lead to duplicate memory on disk and potential differences when loading them again: [{'decoder.tok_emb.weight', 'decoder.head_a.weight'}]. A potential way to correctly save your model is to use `save_model`.

honest_c3: C3-1: Shim source has internal contradiction — line 38/354/451-452/597 explicitly model and configure tie_word_embeddings=True between tok_emb and head_a, but line 643 calls safetensors_save() directly on a wrapped state_dict that still contains both keys with shared storage. safetensors's strict shared-memory check rejects this. The shim self-comment at error site even quotes the safetensors guidance ('use save_model'), so this is a known-pattern bug, not an environment quirk.

C3-2: Loaded param_count (477,648,512) is 53.3M LESS than the dry-run expected (530,994,816). This is a significant discrepancy that the shim did NOT flag as a failure — execution proceeded past load. Either the expected_param_count constant in the shim is mis-specified, OR best.pt is missing tensor groups we expected (e.g., the second head head_g, ca_rules, purefield projection) — this needs investigation before any base-validation, because lm-eval against a 477M model is NOT the same as validating a 530M architecture.

C3-3: Output dir contains .py files (configuration_clm_v4, modeling_clm_v4, conscious_decoder, decoder_v3, __init__) and config.json + generation_config.json, but is missing model.safetensors AND all tokenizer files (tokenizer.model, tokenizer_config.json, special_tokens_map.json). Even if we hand-patched safetensors save, tokenizer copy is downstream of safetensors save in the shim, so the output is unusable for AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(). Two independent fixes are needed in the shim, not one.

C3-4: Scope says 'do not modify shim source'. With that constraint, OPT-1 cannot complete on this shim revision; it requires either (a) BG-Β to ship clm_v4_hf_format_shim.py v2 with model.save_pretrained() (or explicit head_a.weight = head_a.weight.clone() before save_file) plus tokenizer-copy reordering, or (b) explicit user authorization to allow this BG-Δ to fix the shim. No silent workaround attempted.

C3-5: Wall time 22s — far below the 30-60min estimate — because the failure is at save-time, not load-time. The 5GB torch.load DID complete in ~10-15s (decoder loaded message appears), so the shim is computationally healthy; the bug is purely serialization-format. This makes a re-run after a shim-v2 patch fast (~1-2 min total) — low cost to retry once unblocked.
